sources.entry: GitX - Graphical client for the git version control system.

summary.one_liner: GitX is a native macOS graphical client for the git version control system, maintained as a community fork of the original project.
summary.what_it_does: GitX is an OS X (macOS) native graphical front end for git. The README says the GitX GitHub org and repo aim to consolidate the project's various past branches and versions into one current, community-maintained version. It can be installed via Homebrew cask or from the Releases page, with a separate arm64 build for Apple Silicon. It reads and writes SHA-1 repositories using either the files or reftable reference backend, including bare repositories and linked worktrees, without converting reference storage on open. SHA-256 repositories are not supported. For command-line operations it expects Git 2.45 or newer, selected in Preferences. Building is done with a Makefile (make bootstrap, build, unit-test, dmg) and Xcode, and it links the ObjectiveGit and libgit2 dependencies as submodules.
use_cases: browse and manage git repositories visually
work with reftable git repositories on macos
build a macOS git app from source
notable: Native macOS app, installable with a single Homebrew cask command that also puts the gitx CLI on PATH
Supports reftable reference storage for SHA-1 repositories, including bare repos and linked worktrees
Community-maintained consolidation of several earlier GitX branches
Makefile wraps the CI commands for build, unit tests and DMG creation
caveats: Command-line operations need Git 2.45 or newer; older bundled Git versions lack reftable support
Signing with a personal certificate is needed for hardened runtime builds and make dmg-signed; a fresh clone needs make bootstrap first
